methods.label: Let the month determine the day
methods.sourceMethod: Use parity of digit counts, organizing the exhaustive cases by month rather than by the repeated digit.

annotationRationale: Parity determines the required day digits, and disjoint month cases give an exhaustive count. Calendar restrictions supply the supporting validity checks.

classificationReview.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no repair is needed.

review.questionCheck: The valid dates are 01/13, 01/31, 02/23, 03/11, 03/22, 10/13, 10/31, 11/03 and 11/30. There are nine, matching choice E and the key. The supplied shared-question record agrees; no figure or grading contradiction is present.
review.alternativeMethodCheck: The references organize the same parity constraints by the repeated digit. The candidate's month organization is exhaustive and equally accessible, so retaining another case arrangement is unnecessary.
review.annotationCheck: Odd/even digit counts and disjoint counting cases are appropriate assessed concepts. Calendar validity is correctly supporting knowledge rather than the main demand.
review.areaCheck: Counting & Probability is correct; no repair is needed.

methodReviews.mathCheck: Months 04 through 09 require days 3k or k3, all exceeding 31; month 12 leaves four odd counts and is impossible. Months 01 and 10 contribute four dates, 02 contributes one, 03 contributes two, and 11 contributes two. Equal-digit days in March are only 11 and 22 because 00 is invalid and 33 exceeds the month length. The disjoint total is nine.
methodReviews.sourceMethodCheck: The parity observation and resulting dates agree with LIVE and Random Math. Organizing the proof by month gives an independently structured explanation rather than reproducing the references' repeated-digit cases. The third-party classification is accurate.
methodReviews.pedagogyCheck: The rules for repairing zero, two or four odd counts explain the difficult transition. The elimination step and remaining month list visibly cover all twelve months, with legal day checks.
methodReviews.directNodeCheck: cnm_p156 supports identifying odd and even occurrence counts; the explanation supplies the simple parity-update reasoning. cnm_h230 precisely captures adding disjoint month cases, and cnm_p091 supports calendar restrictions.

nativeLayerJudgments.CN: The three exact native links fit parity recognition, addition across cases and calendar validity. The counting strategy extends the elementary parity recognition rather than demonstrating an additional national parity theorem.
nativeLayerJudgments.US: Only cnm_p156 has a supplied US link, partial 2.OA.C.3. It overlaps odd/even recognition for these small counts, but does not cover the full month-case argument or establish the standard's equation requirement. No US links are supplied for case addition or calendar knowledge.
nativeLayerJudgments.ailleo: All three immediate nodes are used with appropriate assessed and support roles. No broad probability node is substituted for the actual counting argument.
